name: rwlock
algorithm: t workers (Mk: tasks; Go: goroutines; Rust and Zig: OS threads) share one pair under the standard reader-writer lock; each does n operations: every tenth (i % 10 == 0) takes the write lock and adds one to both fields, the others take the read lock and count a pair whose fields differ. Prints the first field (t * ceil(n / 10)) and the mismatches (0) (README.md).

skip.c: no reader-writer lock in standard C (C11 <threads.h> has mtx_t only; pthread_rwlock_t is POSIX, SRWLOCK is Win32)
skip.mk-wrap: the only arithmetic is the counters, which stay below 2^40

no_counts: B24 does not apply: the checksum, the final count and no mismatch, shows that every write landed once and no read saw a write in progress
notes: Concurrency row (B19): every column runs on logical CPUs 0, 2, ..., 14 (mask 0x5555, eight physical cores, one logical CPU each) with 8 threads (MK_CARRIERS=8, GOMAXPROCS=8). Rust and Zig use OS threads (their std has no tasks), labelled so.
Written by std-missing (status/std-missing.md, M6 session 2); checksums from the workload's arithmetic, printed by the Mk build on the owner's machine, 2026-11-07.
